newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade students blockade second police cordon.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade students blockade second police cordon.

text.p: Student protesters in Belgrade blockaded a second police cordon on Thursday after forcing police to back off at another location.

Student leaders said they would continue their action until an official statement was issued saying police would not block the streets, and appealed to the people of Belgrade to come out and support them throughout the night.

The students have organised groups of demonstrators to rotate every hour and vow their "24 hours on the street -- them or us" protest will continue until police who have blocked their daily protest marches let them pass.
Police at the first location for the protest dismantled their cordon, but they remained in place in a street near Belgrade's ancient castle, where about 200 students lined up in front of them.
Thursday marked the 53rd day of protests against the cancellation of local election results by President Slobodan Milosevic's ruling Socialists last November.
On Wednesday, Milosevic conceded that Zajedno had won in Nis, Serbia's second city, but Zajedno leaders vowed protests would continue until all their claims were met.

"We demand our election results down to the very last mandate and there is no reason for us to give a single seat to the red thieves," one Zajedno leader, Zoran Djindjic, told the rally of about 20,000 people in Republic Square.
"The people of Nis said that if the November 17 elections results are not recognised by January 14 ,they will get into 2,000 or 3,000 cars and travel to Belgrade."
